section_summary.extract_value: This section describes data analysis procedures including handling of missing data, manipulation checks, ANCOVA tests, and mediation analyses using a structural equation model with the counterfactual method to allow for treatment–mediator interaction. Missing data procedures included mean substitution for a few item-level misses, FIML for mediation analyses, and EM imputation for ANCOVA; covariates (trait body anxiety and post-test negative emotions) were included in the mediation model.
section_summary.evidence_source: "There was no missing data on the posttest measures of body anxiety or guilt." "The counterfactual method detailed by Muthén and Asparouhov (2015; see also Valeri & Vanderweele, 2013) was employed to examine this possibility, allowing the simultaneous consideration of the mediation and treatment–mediator interaction."

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes data handling and analysis procedures for the (labelled) study, noting missing-data handling (mean substitution for a few items, EM algorithm for ANCOVA, FIML for mediation) and use of 2×2 ANOVAs and ANCOVAs for manipulation checks and overall effects. It details the use of counterfactual structural equation modeling to test mediation by post-test guilt including treatment–mediator interaction, and states that trait body anxiety and post-test negative emotions were included as covariates. The table asset provided is labelled as pertaining to 'Study 2'.
section_summary.evidence_source:
Key sentences: 'There was no missing data on the posttest measures of body anxiety or guilt... these were replaced by mean substitution... For the pre-test measure of trait body anxiety, however, there was missing data on just under 10% of cases (16 out of N = 165).'
'Manipulation checks were conducted using a 2 × 2 analysis of variance (ANOVA). Tests for the overall effects of the manipulations... were conducted using an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA)'.
'The counterfactual method detailed by Muthén and Asparouhov (2015)... was employed to examine this possibility... We therefore included two variables as covariates of post-test guilt and post-test body anxiety: trait body anxiety and post-test negative emotions (the mean of five negative emotions from the I-PANAS-SF).'
Table caption: 'Table 3 ... (Study 2).'
